question: Why does a roughly 22 ms CPU prefetch window contain only 9.57 ms of GPU memcpy, and why does GPU capture end near Perfetto second 48?

configuration_profile.source_role: Read-only analysis of hash-verified retained raw artifacts; no new serving run

change: English GPU stream labels and decode/prefill event names without sched prefixes.
Preserve CPU timing identity in an explicit timing_scope property; profile routing and gap detection use this property.
Only encoder-bearing prefill records carry the +encoder label.
Regenerate Perfetto and HTML in the english-labels presentation variant; remove superseded presentation artifacts after validation, retain all raw evidence.

focus_transfer.interpretation: Most excess wall time precedes device memcpy and lies in host submission, not the CopyService queue or the completion callback. Submission overlaps the start of DMA; do not add submission duration and full DMA duration as disjoint phases.

submission_localization.gap_scope: Between return of start cudaEventRecordWithFlags and the next cudaStreamIsCapturing before the end event; surrounds descriptor preparation and the batch-copy call.

CPU_preparation_probe.method: Same installed copy_blocks with _batch_memcpy_fn replaced by a no-op; synthetic 128-block descriptors, total 917504 bytes per block, 30 warmups then 100 samples; no CUDA transfer or allocation. Does not replay the original thread schedule.

submission_localization.post_capture_observation: Host submission remains millisecond-scale after capture ends; examples transfer 187: 14.694 ms for 148635648 bytes and transfer 192: 14.567 ms for 150470656 bytes. Different sizes and conditions, not a controlled profiler on/off comparison.
submission_localization.inference: Small descriptor-construction cost supports batch-copy submission or scheduling within that call as the dominant remaining candidate. Existing capture omits a cuMemcpyBatchAsync CPU API span, so driver processing, profiling overhead and host scheduling cannot be separately quantified.

capture.stop_path: Worker _capture_gpu_activity awaits gpu_trace_start, sleeps the configured eight seconds, then calls gpu_trace_stop. EngineCore utility synchronously calls profiler.stop and export_chrome_trace.
capture.interpretation: The endpoint is a configured short diagnostic window, not a CUDA tracing limit or GPU idle boundary. Stopping inside the business phase perturbs serving; this run does not provide full-run GPU coverage.

validation.render: Chromium loaded local HTML without page errors; three English GPU lanes, eight CPU scheduler lanes, decode/prefill colors and gap detection verified
validation.event_preservation: All 136563 events preserve pid/tid/ph/time/duration; GPU bytes and attribution unchanged.

remaining_uncertainty: The raw profiler has no CPU cuMemcpyBatchAsync duration. The root is localized to submission, but attributing its whole wall interval solely to CUDA driver execution would exceed the evidence.
The CPU preparation probe is not an isolated serving replay or a performance finding. No GPU replay was started while all devices were occupied.
No runtime copy optimization or full-business GPU capture was implemented; presentation changes do not remove profiler-stop overhead.
